newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Satellite phone service launched in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Satellite phone service launched in Nigeria.

text.p: New hope of an improvement to Nigeria's dire internal telecommunications arrived on Friday with the launch of a domestic satellite service aimed at business.

The service is provided by Omnes Communications, the Nigerian subsidiary of Omnes Worldwide, which is jointly owned by British company Cable and Wireless Plc and American oil services company Schlumberger.
Omnes Worldwide chief executive Jean Chevallier said, "Launching this OMSAT service here is the first step in turning Nigeria into Africa's business centre.
"Nigeria's telecommunications sector has high potential and our aim is to provide double communications solutions for Africa via Nigeria."
Telecommunications in Africa's most populous nation of 100 million people have been notoriously difficult. Telephone lines are frequently cut off for technical or bureaucratic reasons.
But the sector, until now operated by state-run monopoly NITEL (Nigerian Telecommunications), is slowly opening up to private enterprise.
NITEL in July signed inter-connectivity agreements with five firms. But the five, which have been given provisional licences, are yet to start operations.
DOMSAT is targetted initially at multinational oil companies and banks.
Managing director of the Nigerian subsidiary, Jonathan Powell, said a big multinational oil company is the first subscriber for the service. He declined to name the company.
He said Omnes planned to begin with services for about 400 customers and had set a target of 1,000 at full capacity.
A demonstration of the DOMSAT service at the launch showed it would offer high speed exchange of voice and data messages among subscribers.
"Subscribers are assured that this DOMSAT service, which costs over $2 million, installed in July and run and managed by Nigerians, will work daily and be properly maintained," Powell said.
Other services planned by Omnes for Nigeria include international electronic mail, cellular telephones, Internet access and maintenance of telecommunications facilities.
"We will launch all our other services for other businesses as and when due," Powell said.
